02The clock

Most studios promise deliverables next quarter. We ship yours by Thursday.

THU→

Last deploy: Thursday [date]

You know the pattern. A six-week discovery phase. A kickoff deck. Status calls where the honest answer is "we're still setting up the environment." A demo in month four that looks nothing like what you described.

We run on a different clock.

Scope is locked in week one. From week two, there is a working build in your hands every Thursday: deployed, clickable, on a real URL, not a Figma frame. A focused MVP is live in eight weeks. A multi-tenant platform with third-party integrations and a compliance layer runs 10 to 14.

We tell you which one you are during the Build Review, in writing, before there is a contract to sign. The eight weeks on our homepage is a commitment, not a range we hope you forget.

You will never have to ask what we're working on. You'll be using it.

03What we stand on

01 · Enterprise standard, from commit one

Multi-tenant architecture. Role-based access control. Audit logging. Encryption in transit and at rest. Automated CI/CD, real test coverage, documented APIs, infrastructure as code.

Most MVPs are demos with a database behind them, and they get thrown away the moment you get traction. Ours are the first version of the system you'll still be running at Series B.

We build the thing you scale, not the thing you replace.

02 · Designed like a product, not a project

Your first users, your first investors, and your first enterprise buyer all form their opinion in about four seconds. We don't hand that moment to a template.

Every build ships with a real design system: typography, motion, states, empty states, error states, dark mode where it matters. Interfaces our clients' customers assume were made by a fifteen-person in-house team.

Nobody should be able to tell it's version one.

03 · Shipped on a clock, not a hope

Fixed scope. Weekly deploys. A named senior engineer and a founder who answers directly, not an account manager relaying messages across a time zone.

If we miss a Thursday, you hear about it Wednesday, with the reason and the new date.

That's the whole relationship in one sentence.

05What we don’t do

We don't run six-week discovery phases and call them progress.

We don't bolt a chatbot onto a sidebar. If a model isn't the right answer for the problem, we'll say so on the call.

We don't quote a number we can't hold. If your scope is a twelve-week scope, you'll hear twelve, and you'll hear it before you sign.

We don't hold your code. It lives in your repository, under your account, from the first commit.

06Process

Four steps. No mystery.

01

Scope

The Build Review · Week 0

Before anyone signs a build contract, we do the work. Two weeks of real technical and product diligence: architecture recommendation, scope and sequencing, integration and compliance risks, a build plan, and a launch date.

You keep everything, whether or not you hire us to build it. If you take it to another studio, it makes them better too. We're comfortable with that. Most clients don't take it anywhere.

02

Shape

Scope lock and design direction · Week 1

We agree on exactly what version one is, and what it isn't. You approve a design direction before we write feature code. Nothing after this is a surprise.

03

Ship

Thursday deploys · Week 2 through launch

A deployed build every Thursday. A short Loom walking through what changed. Direct access to the team in your Slack.

04

Scale

Launch and beyond

We handle deployment, app store submission, monitoring, and handover. Then either you take the keys, with full code ownership and documentation and no lock-in, or we stay on as your product team.

08FAQ

Questions,
answered.

Is eight weeks real, or is that a marketing number?

It's real, and it's specific: eight weeks from scope lock to live, for a focused MVP with a defined feature set. What moves that number is integration surface and compliance requirements. A multi-tenant platform wired into third-party systems runs 10 to 14 weeks. You get your actual date during the Build Review, before you commit to a build. We'd rather lose the deal on a longer honest estimate than win it on a date we miss.

Where is your team?

Our engineering team is in Bengaluru. Our engagements run on US hours with committed daily overlap for Eastern and Central time zones, and your founder contact is available in your working day.

Do you work with non-technical founders?

Most of our clients are operators and domain experts, not engineers. You bring the market knowledge. We bring the technical judgment, including telling you when the thing you asked for isn't the thing you need.

Will my MVP actually be scalable, or will we rebuild it in a year?

This is the one we care most about. Every build ships with production architecture: proper data modeling, tenant isolation, migrations, monitoring, test coverage. The purpose of shipping fast is to learn fast, not to accumulate debt you pay off with a rewrite.

What if we already have a team?

Then we augment rather than replace. We take a defined workstream, ship it to the same standard, and hand it over documented.

What happens if we want to leave mid-build?

Milestone-based contracts have defined exit points. You leave with everything built to that point, in your repository, documented.
